newsitem.title: SWEDEN: British Airways can't rule out more Nordic moves.
newsitem.headline: British Airways can't rule out more Nordic moves.

text.p: British Airways PLC chief executive Bob Ayling said on Tuesday he would not rule out more moves by the carrier in Nordic skies.
British Airways already has a close relationship with Denmark's Maersk airline, a franchise agreement with Sun Air of Denmark, and its frequent flier programme is linked to Norway's Braathens SAFE.
"I wouldn't like to say that's the end of developments in that area, but I am not announcing any changes today," Ayling told a news conference.
He called the region a natural market for British companies and said the carrier had plans in the pipeline for Scandinavia.
"We compete head-to-head now with SAS here. We have very strong expansion plans both for domestic and international flights," Ayling said.
"We see the Scandinavian market, and in particular the Swedish market, as being a natural market for a company which is based in northern Europe."
Regarding its proposed alliance with American Airlines, Ayling said the airline was waiting for a decision from the British government but said he expected a final word by June.

"I would be very surprised if the regulatory process -- that is the bilateral and the competition process -- is not finished by June. (But) Nothing will start again until after the election," he said.
